newsitem.title: UK: Celltech says new drug test encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Celltech says new drug test encouraging.

text.p: Celltech said a study of the effects of its leukaemia drug CMA 676 were "encouraging", showing the drug was remarkably safe.
"This means that CMA 676 is potentially suitable for out-patient use," Celltech said.
A study covering 36 refractory patients suffering from acute mykeloid leukaemia in two U.S. centres showed the main side effect were fever and chills for short periods.
Two patients responded completely to the treatment, while three partial responses were achieved. One patient achieved a full response for four months before relapsing again.
The patients taking part had generally failed several existing treatments previously.
The main object of this study was therefore to determine a maximum tolerated dose. The study showed the safety profile of CMA 676 was "quite remarkable".

"This result is particularly important because it means that if CMA 676 is approved for therapy it can be used in an out-patient setting making the treatment much more convenient for patients," Celltech said.
Another study in about 10 U.S. and Canadian centres in 50 first relapse patients are planned for early 1997.
"It is expected that these patients will be more responsive to treatment that the refractory group," Celltech said.
It added the new study could support accelerated registration of CMA 676.
Further studies will also be undertaken in Europe.
Shares in the company were up 12 1/2p at 500p by 0805 GMT.
